# Editor-resolved parallel build job limit, supplied via -D on every editor
# configure. Declared here so it is documented and so CMake does not warn
# about an unused variable on generators that do not consume it (only the
# MSVC branch below reads it). Empty or 0 means no per-file compile limit.
set(QUANTUM_PARALLEL_BUILD_JOBS "" CACHE STRING "Editor-resolved parallel build job limit")

# Build mode: when ON, build as Quantum Editor plugin (shared library)

add_compile_definitions(QUANTUM_PHYSICS_2D QUANTUM_PHYSICS_3D JPH_OBJECT_LAYER_BITS=32)

if(QUANTUM_EDITOR_PLUGIN)
    if(NOT WIN32 OR NOT (MSVC OR CMAKE_CXX_SIMULATE_ID STREQUAL "MSVC"))
        message(FATAL_ERROR "This Quantum editor requires MSVC-compatible C++ plugins. MSYS2/MinGW GCC cannot link its engine library. Select an MSVC-compatible compiler in Editor Settings > Desktop, or rebuild the editor and engine with your MinGW toolchain.")
    endif()
    if(NOT CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P EQUAL 8)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "C++ plugins must match this Quantum editor's 64-bit architecture. Select a matching compiler in Editor Settings > Desktop.")
    endif()
endif()

if(QUANTUM_EDITOR_PLUGIN)
    add_compile_definitions(QUANTUM_EDITOR_PLUGIN)
    # The editor links its own engine build, which is compiled as a shared
    # library with editor-specific data layouts. The plugin must match both:
    #  - QUANTUM_SHARED makes QUANTUM_API resolve to __declspec(dllimport) so
    #    static members such as Engine::onUpdate link against the import lib on MSVC.
    #  - QUANTUM_EDITOR keeps HybridArray (and other editor-only layouts)
    #    ABI-compatible across the DLL boundary.
    #  - JPH_SHARED_LIBRARY does the same as QUANTUM_SHARED for Jolt.
    add_compile_definitions(QUANTUM_SHARED QUANTUM_EDITOR JPH_SHARED_LIBRARY)
endif()

# Every translation unit linking the engine DLL needs the CRT that DLL was built
# with: debug and release STL disagree on std::string/std::vector layout and use
# separate heaps, and an import library carries no /FAILIFMISMATCH records, so
# the linker cannot catch the mismatch. The build type cannot pick it either,
# since IDEs default to Debug, so it follows the editor that generated this file.
if(MSVC AND NOT DEFINED CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY)
    set(CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY "MultiThreadedDebugDLL")
endif()

    # Each desktop OS uses the same native application backend as the editor,
    # compiled from the engine API snapshot in ${INTERNAL_DIR}/engine-api.
    if(NOT QUANTUM_GRAPHIC_BACKEND)
        set(QUANTUM_GRAPHIC_BACKEND "glcore")
    endif()


    # FindVulkan reads the VULKAN_SDK environment variable the SDK installer sets
    macro(quantum_find_vulkan)
        # sokol_gfx binds every resource through VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer, which
        # MoltenVK does not implement, so the build only fails at device selection
        if(APPLE)
            message(WARNING "QUANTUM_GRAPHIC_BACKEND=vulkan runs on MoltenVK here, which does not implement VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer: this build will fail at startup unless the driver provides it. QUANTUM_GRAPHIC_BACKEND=metal is the working macOS backend.")
        endif()

        # An app started from the Dock inherits no shell environment, so on macOS
        # the SDK is also looked for where its installer unpacks it
        if(APPLE AND NOT DEFINED ENV{VULKAN_SDK})
            file(GLOB quantumVulkanSdkDirs "$ENV{HOME}/VulkanSDK/*/macOS")
            if(quantumVulkanSdkDirs)
                list(SORT quantumVulkanSdkDirs)
                list(POP_BACK quantumVulkanSdkDirs quantumVulkanSdkNewest)
                set(ENV{VULKAN_SDK} "${quantumVulkanSdkNewest}")
            endif()
        endif()
        find_package(Vulkan QUIET)
        if(NOT Vulkan_FOUND)
            message(FATAL_ERROR "QUANTUM_GRAPHIC_BACKEND=vulkan needs the Vulkan SDK (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/sdk/home), and VULKAN_SDK is not set here. If it is installed outside the default location, restart the shell or editor this build was started from with VULKAN_SDK in its environment: Windows only gives the variable to processes started after the installer ran. Otherwise use QUANTUM_GRAPHIC_BACKEND=glcore, or metal on macOS.")
        endif()
    endmacro()

    set(QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR ${QUANTUM_API_DIR}/platform)

            ${QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR}/mac/main.mm
        )
        list(APPEND PLATFORM_LIBS "-framework Cocoa" "-framework QuartzCore" "-framework GameController")
        # MTKView has no GL or Vulkan drawable, so those get views of their own

            add_definitions("-DSOKOL_GLCORE")
            list(APPEND PLATFORM_SOURCE ${QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR}/mac/MacViewGL.mm)
            list(APPEND PLATFORM_LIBS "-framework OpenGL")
        elseif(QUANTUM_GRAPHIC_BACKEND STREQUAL "vulkan")
            add_definitions("-DSOKOL_VULKAN")
            add_definitions("-DVK_USE_PLATFORM_METAL_EXT")
            list(APPEND PLATFORM_SOURCE ${QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR}/mac/MacViewVulkan.mm ${QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR}/common/VulkanContext.cpp)

        else()
            add_definitions("-DSOKOL_METAL")
            list(APPEND PLATFORM_SOURCE ${QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR}/mac/MacViewMetal.mm)
            list(APPEND PLATFORM_LIBS "-framework Metal" "-framework MetalKit")
        endif()
    else()
        find_package(X11 REQUIRED)
        list(APPEND PLATFORM_SOURCE
            ${QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR}/linux/QuantumLinux.cpp
            ${QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR}/linux/WindowLinux.cpp
            ${QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR}/linux/SystemLinux.cpp
            ${QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR}/linux/LinuxInputRouter.cpp
            ${QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR}/linux/GamepadLinux.cpp
            ${QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR}/linux/GamepadDB.cpp
        )
        list(APPEND PLATFORM_LIBS X11::X11 dl m)
        if(QUANTUM_GRAPHIC_BACKEND STREQUAL "vulkan")
            add_definitions("-DSOKOL_VULKAN")
            add_definitions("-DVK_USE_PLATFORM_XLIB_KHR")
            list(APPEND PLATFORM_SOURCE ${QUANTUM_PLATFORM_DIR}/common/VulkanContext.cpp)
            quantum_find_vulkan()

# libquantum is searched in QUANTUM_LIB_DIR, in this order: -DQUANTUM_LIB_DIR=...,
# the QUANTUM_LIB_DIR environment variable (the global knob that points every
# project at one engine build tree), then QUANTUM_DEFAULT_LIB_DIR, the Quantum
# editor executable directory recorded in LocalPaths.cmake when the project
# was last opened.
include(${INTERNAL_DIR}/LocalPaths.cmake OPTIONAL)
if(NOT DEFINED QUANTUM_LIB_DIR OR QUANTUM_LIB_DIR STREQUAL "")
    if(DEFINED ENV{QUANTUM_LIB_DIR} AND NOT "$ENV{QUANTUM_LIB_DIR}" STREQUAL "")
        file(TO_CMAKE_PATH "$ENV{QUANTUM_LIB_DIR}" QUANTUM_LIB_DIR)
    else()
        set(QUANTUM_LIB_DIR "${QUANTUM_DEFAULT_LIB_DIR}")
    endif()
    # Default target is the editor's own engine build (shared, editor layouts).
    # Match its macros so symbols link (QUANTUM_SHARED, JPH_SHARED_LIBRARY -> dllimport on MSVC)
    # and data layouts stay ABI-compatible (QUANTUM_EDITOR), avoiding ODR/ABI mismatch.
    add_compile_definitions(QUANTUM_SHARED QUANTUM_EDITOR JPH_SHARED_LIBRARY)
endif()

# Find quantum library in specified location. find_library() caches its
# result, so a stale QUANTUM_LIB from a previous configure (e.g. before the
# editor/engine install moved) would otherwise stick around unchanged;
# force a fresh search on every configure instead.
unset(QUANTUM_LIB CACHE)
find_library(QUANTUM_LIB NAMES quantum PATHS "${QUANTUM_LIB_DIR}" NO_DEFAULT_PATH)
if(NOT QUANTUM_LIB)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "Quantum library not found in ${QUANTUM_LIB_DIR}")
endif()

target_link_libraries(FPS_Template PRIVATE ${QUANTUM_LIB} ${PLATFORM_LIBS})

# Set compile options based on compiler and platform
if(MSVC)
    # C4251/C4275: exported engine classes (QUANTUM_API -> dllimport) expose STL
    # members (std::vector, std::string, FunctionSubscribe, ...). This is safe
    # here because the engine DLL and this plugin use the same dynamic CRT/STL,
    # so suppress the dll-interface warnings that would otherwise flood the build.
    # MSBuild's /m only parallelizes projects. /MP applies the editor-resolved
    # limit to translation units within this single-target plugin project.
    # /utf-8: generated sources embed UTF-8 literals and carry no BOM, so
    # MSVC would otherwise decode them in the active code page.
    if(DEFINED QUANTUM_PARALLEL_BUILD_JOBS AND QUANTUM_PARALLEL_BUILD_JOBS GREATER 0)
        target_compile_options(FPS_Template PRIVATE /W4 /EHsc /utf-8 /MP${QUANTUM_PARALLEL_BUILD_JOBS} /wd4251 /wd4275)
    else()
        target_compile_options(FPS_Template PRIVATE /W4 /EHsc /utf-8 /MP /wd4251 /wd4275)
    endif()
else()
    target_compile_options(FPS_Template PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -fPIC)
    # Error on unresolved symbols at link time. Apple ld does this by default;
    # GNU ld needs '-z defs --no-undefined' and MinGW only understands '--no-undefined'.
    if(WIN32)
        target_link_options(FPS_Template PRIVATE -Wl,--no-undefined)
    elseif(NOT APPLE)
        target_link_options(FPS_Template PRIVATE -Wl,-z,defs,--no-undefined)
    endif()
endif()

# Set properties for the shared library
set_target_properties(FPS_Template PROPERTIES
    RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_DEBUG ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}
    RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_RELEASE ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}
    RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_RELWITHDEBINFO ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}
    RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_MINSIZEREL ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}
    LIBRARY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_DEBUG ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}
    LIBRARY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_RELEASE ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}
    LIBRARY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_RELWITHDEBINFO ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}
    LIBRARY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_MINSIZEREL ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}
    OUTPUT_NAME "FPS_Template"
    PREFIX ""
)

# The engine DLL lives next to the editor, and Windows searches only the
# executable directory and PATH, so a standalone build needs its own copy or
# it dies with STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND before main(). The other desktops get
# QUANTUM_LIB_DIR in the build rpath from CMake.
if(WIN32 AND NOT QUANTUM_EDITOR_PLUGIN)
    # Same reason as QUANTUM_LIB above: never reuse a cached path
    unset(QUANTUM_RUNTIME_LIB CACHE)
    find_file(QUANTUM_RUNTIME_LIB NAMES quantum.dll PATHS "${QUANTUM_LIB_DIR}" NO_DEFAULT_PATH)
    if(QUANTUM_RUNTIME_LIB)
        add_custom_command(TARGET FPS_Template POST_BUILD
            COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different
                    "${QUANTUM_RUNTIME_LIB}" "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:FPS_Template>"
            COMMENT "Copying the Quantum engine runtime next to the executable")
    else()
        message(WARNING "quantum.dll not found in ${QUANTUM_LIB_DIR}: the executable will not start outside the editor.")
    endif()
endif()

# Optional user build file, never written by the editor: extra include roots,
# libraries and defines go there so they survive regeneration. Attach to
# QUANTUM_TARGET, not the literal target name, and use QUANTUM_SCRIPTS_DIR as the
# root of script paths; the exported build sets both, so one file serves either.
set(QUANTUM_TARGET FPS_Template)
set(QUANTUM_SCRIPTS_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR})
include(${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/ProjectBuild.cmake OPTIONAL)
